newsitem.title: USA: Mother, boyfriend indicted in NY child's murder.
newsitem.headline: Mother, boyfriend indicted in NY child's murder.

text.p: In a case that prompted changes in the way New York City tries to protect children from abuse, the mother of a slain 8-year-old girl was indicted Monday on charges of covering up the murder for a year.

Denise Solero, 29, agreed to testify against her former boyfriend, Luis Santiago, 24, who authorities alleged tried to drown the girl in a bathtub before he beat her with a metal rod and then suffocated her on New Year's Eve 1995.

An indictment was also filed Monday charging Santiago with murdering Justina Morales, whose body has still not been found. Santiago faces life in prison if convicted on the second degree murder charges.
Solero was indicted Monday on a charge of hindering the prosecution by giving criminal assistance to Santiago.

The girl's death led the city's Administration for Children's Services to initiate new procedures and training to make sure that communications are improved between the agency and the city Board of Education.

"This tragedy illustrates a very important point that excessive absences repeatedly over a period of time are a warning sign," said Edward Stancik, special commissioner of investigation for the city school district. "A parent who will consistently neglect his child's education is at risk of physically abusing that child as well. So repeated absences are a warning and those warnings need to be heeded."
The grand jury that heard the case against Solero will also hear testimony about reforms regarding notification procedures of schoolchildren.

"We won't rely on the occasional attendance officer reporting information to us or the caseworker having to ferret it out through a number of phone calls, we will have it at our fingertips," ACS Commissioner Nicholas Scoppetta said.

When investigators inquired about the child's whereabouts, the couple told people she was living with her natural father in Alabama. Solero has already pleaded guilty to one count of hindering the prosecution.
